references.text: Reiterates that the Israelites are God's servants whom he brought out of Egypt, and therefore belong to him.
The basis for God's claim on Israel: He brought them out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
Reminder that Israel was a slave in Egypt and was redeemed by the Lord, as the foundation for how they should treat others.
Laws concerning Hebrew slaves and their release, showing that Israelites were not to be permanent slaves.
The Lord brought Israel out of Egypt and redeemed them from the house of slavery.
The Lord gave Egypt as a ransom for Israel, demonstrating his ownership over his people.
Believers are bought with a price and should not become slaves of men, reflecting the principle from Leviticus.
Believers were redeemed by Christ's precious blood, not with silver or gold, fulfilling the theme of redemption.
